tasks.task: Duplicate / double charge
tasks.example: I was charged twice at Shell
tasks.outcome: Reads the ledger, separates a pending hold from a real duplicate, files a dispute with provisional credit ≤ $500 when asked

tasks.task: Large duplicate or customer who does not meet the auto conditions
tasks.outcome: Dispute filed as pending; a human approves the provisional credit; the customer is told it is pending

tasks.task: Transfer not arrived / pending / returned
tasks.outcome: Traces the transfer, applies the rail timing policy, explains return codes; overdue transfers go to a human

tasks.task: Cancel a transfer
tasks.example: Cancel the transfer I just made
tasks.outcome: Only a pending, unsubmitted transfer; wires are irrevocable and refused with the reason

tasks.task: Fee reversal
tasks.example: Can you waive the overdraft fee?
tasks.outcome: One courtesy waiver per 12 months up to $35; above that a human decides

tasks.task: Explain a fee, a pending payment or a statement line
tasks.outcome: Quotes the real ledger rows and the policy

tasks.task: Payment the customer does not recognise
tasks.outcome: Checks location, velocity, merchant risk, history and alerts: block + dispute + replacement on fraud signals; refuses a known merchant

tasks.task: Lost or stolen card
tasks.outcome: Blocks the card immediately on request (protective); offers a replacement; zero liability

tasks.task: Declined payment
tasks.outcome: Reads the decline reason from the ledger and explains the fix

tasks.task: Replacement card
tasks.outcome: Only for a blocked, lost or expired card; idempotent

tasks.task: Limits, PIN, activation, ATM, contactless how-to
tasks.example: How do I change my PIN?
tasks.outcome: Answered from the help articles and the policy table

tasks.task: Products, rates, accounts, identity checks, support hours
tasks.outcome: Answered from the help articles only

tasks.task: Angry or abusive customer
tasks.outcome: Holding reply with reference + ETA; case in the queue

tasks.task: Legal threat or formal complaint
tasks.outcome: Critical / high priority; no admissions or promises

tasks.task: Account takeover, scam or identity theft
tasks.example: Someone got into my online banking
tasks.outcome: Security queue, critical; the customer is told not to share PINs or codes

tasks.task: Bereavement, closed or frozen account, questions about reviews of wires
tasks.outcome: Never auto-resolved; compliance topics are never discussed with the customer

tasks.task: Customer asks for a person / repeat contact
tasks.example: Let me talk to a manager
tasks.outcome: Always honoured; ≥3 open tickets AND a complaint signal

tasks.task: Verification says 'human', or the system cannot answer safely
tasks.outcome: Uncertain, ungrounded or rejected drafts are held for a human

tasks.task: Off-topic, jailbreak, prompt injection, other customers' data
tasks.outcome: Polite refusal; security event logged

tasks.task: SQL injection
tasks.outcome: Refused in milliseconds; queries are parameterised anyway

out_of_scope: Moving real money: refunds, provisional credits and fee reversals are ledger entries in a simulated bank, not payouts on a real payment rail.
Loan, mortgage and investment decisions or advice.
Opening and closing accounts, changing personal details, identity-document checks: guidance only.
Disputes for goods not received or wrong amount (only duplicate and unauthorised disputes are automated).
Languages other than English in escalation templates (specialists reply in the customer's language).

steps.text: Sanitise text; mask card numbers and secrets; SQL-injection and prompt-injection checks
steps.boundary: Customer text enters the system here

steps.text: Intent = payments, urgency, sentiment, action_requested (did the customer ask us to act?)
get_transactions: the ledger rows for the signed-in customer only
steps.boundary: Agent → tool runtime: identity comes from the JWT, never from the model

steps.text: verify_transaction_issue(duplicate_charge): the knowledge graph names the checks and policies; the checks run against the ledger

Checks: same card + merchant + amount within 24 h (POL-DUP-01) → pending hold vs posted (POL-HOLD-01) → already disputed? → dispute window 60 days (POL-DSP-01) → provisional-credit eligibility (POL-DSP-02) → internal flag
steps.boundary: Policy is data in the database, decisions are code

steps.text: Decision 'act' and the customer asked: file_dispute(verification_id); the tool re-derives the decision itself
steps.boundary: Write needs customer intent + a matching verification

steps.text: Above $500, unverified identity or a new account: the dispute is PENDING and a human approves the provisional credit
steps.boundary: Money above the limit needs a person

steps.text: 'Credit issued' only if a credit is posted in the evidence; every id and amount must come from tool results
Delivered with the dispute id and the exact status

workflows.name: Payment the customer does not recognise

steps.text: As W1
Intent = cards; action_requested = true (reporting a payment as not theirs)
get_cards + get_transactions; the transaction is picked from the amount or merchant the customer named

verify_transaction_issue(unrecognised_payment): merchant history, country, velocity (3 in 60 min), merchant risk, fraud-engine alert (score never shown), card status, dispute window, provisional-credit eligibility
Known merchant (paid before) → no_action with the earlier dates; fraud signals → act: block card + dispute + replacement; no signals → dispute only
block_card (protective) then file_dispute(verification_id), then request_replacement_card only if the customer asked
'Card blocked' / 'dispute filed' must be backed by the matching tool result
Delivered
As W1
Intent = cards
get_cards: one active card, or the one the customer named
verify_transaction_issue(lost_stolen_card): POL-LIA-01 zero liability; blocking is always allowed
block_card(card_id): idempotent, audited
request_replacement_card only when asked: only for a blocked, lost or expired card
Delivered
As W1
Intent = payments
get_transfer_status: rail, expected date, return code
verify_transaction_issue(transfer_trace): ACH 1-3 business days (POL-ACH-01), wire same day before 17:00 ET (POL-WIR-01), return-code meaning, was the money returned to the ledger
On time: explains and does nothing. Overdue or return not credited: hand-off to a human
Cancellation: verify_transaction_issue(transfer_cancel) → only pending and not submitted (POL-CAN-01); wires are refused
cancel_transfer(verification_id): releases the held amount
Delivered
As W1
Intent = payments; action_requested = true for 'waive' / 'reverse'
verify_transaction_issue(fee_dispute): fee ≤ $35, no waiver in 12 months, account in good standing, not already credited (POL-FEE-01)
reverse_fee(verification_id): credit + waiver record, idempotent
Denied: explains which rule applied (for example a waiver already used on a date)
Delivered
As W1
Intent = general / payments / cards
search_knowledge_base (40 help articles) and, for exact rules, get_policy; no account data is read for a how-to question
Numbers must appear in the evidence; unsupported 'we don't offer X' claims are blocked
Delivered (validated KB-only answers can be cached)
As W1
Deterministic triggers (legal, formal complaint, account takeover / scam, bereavement, account restriction, explicit human request, anger, repeat contact) override the model
Escalation agent: gathers ticket history, writes an internal handoff note, files the case through assign_to_human
Staff see the case, the draft and the trace; approve, edit or reject
The customer gets a holding reply with a reference and ETA; the graph resumes when staff resolve
Injection score, SQL patterns, other customers' ids: blocked before any model or tool
steps.boundary: The first and cheapest line of defence

steps.text: If something got through: parameterised, customer-scoped queries; a foreign customer id is refused
Last line: PII, other customers' ids, internal risk information and tool names can never appear in a reply
Refused safely

tools.name: search_knowledge_base
tools.purpose: Help-center articles (40 pages)
tools.guards: free-text SQLi scan; ≤4 calls; hidden after a strong prefetch hit; weak matches flagged
tools.on_failure: no relevant article ⇒ agent must say so / hand off

tools.name: get_customer_profile
tools.purpose: Segment, identity-verified, country (never the internal risk flag)
tools.guards: identity from JWT; no id parameter

tools.name: get_accounts
tools.purpose: Accounts with balance and status
tools.guards: WHERE customer_id = session

tools.name: get_transactions
tools.purpose: Ledger rows (days, kind, status, merchant, amount filters)
tools.guards: WHERE customer_id = session; limit ≤ 30

tools.name: get_transaction_detail
tools.purpose: One transaction with merchant, related credits and disputes
tools.guards: id regex + strict SQLi scan; same error for foreign and missing ids

tools.name: get_transfer_status
tools.purpose: Transfers: rail, expected date, return code
tools.guards: WHERE customer_id = session

tools.name: get_cards
tools.purpose: Cards: status, limits, controls
tools.guards: WHERE customer_id = session

tools.name: get_fraud_alerts
tools.purpose: Fraud-engine alerts (signal, status; score hidden)
tools.guards: score column never returned

tools.name: get_policy
tools.purpose: Policy rows by id or keyword, with regulation and help article
tools.guards: compliance policies (AML / KYC) are filtered out

tools.name: query_knowledge_graph
tools.purpose: Checks, policies, regulations, actions for an issue type; or how one of the customer's ids relates to others
tools.guards: customer-scoped operational layer; AML nodes hidden

tools.name: verify_transaction_issue
tools.purpose: THE INVESTIGATOR: KG → checks → ledger + policy table → decision + verification record
tools.guards: pure function of data + policy rows; idempotent per query; internal facts never returned

tools.name: file_dispute
tools.purpose: Files a duplicate / unauthorised dispute; posts provisional credit within the policy limit
tools.guards: customer intent + dispatcher flag; verification required and re-derived; idempotent; audited
tools.on_failure: blocked + security event; model must explain instead

tools.name: reverse_fee
tools.purpose: Reverses a fee as a courtesy waiver
tools.guards: customer intent; verification required; idempotent; audited

tools.name: cancel_transfer
tools.purpose: Cancels a pending, unsubmitted transfer
tools.guards: customer intent; verification required; wires never

tools.name: block_card
tools.purpose: Blocks a card now (lost, stolen, fraud)
tools.guards: customer must report or ask; idempotent; audited

tools.name: request_replacement_card
tools.purpose: Orders a replacement for a blocked, lost or expired card
tools.guards: customer must ask; card state precondition; idempotent

tools.name: get_service_status
tools.purpose: Live status of channels
tools.guards: read-only

tools.name: create_ticket
tools.purpose: Opens a follow-up ticket
tools.guards: only if the customer asks; idempotent for 10 min; audited

tools.name: get_ticket_history
tools.purpose: Recent tickets
tools.guards: WHERE customer_id = session

tools.name: assign_to_human
tools.purpose: Creates the review-queue row
tools.guards: one row per query; PII masked before storage; audited
tools.on_failure: reply falls back to a safe holding message

tools_common: Every call: per-agent allow-list, strict schema, SQLi scan, identity injected from the session, ≤12 calls/query, 10 s timeout, traced span (PII-masked).

agents.name: Input guard
agents.can: Sanitise, mask secrets and card numbers, refuse injection / SQLi / empty input, flag foreign ids
agents.cannot: Call tools, see the profile, produce answers beyond fixed refusals
agents.failure: Regexes are deterministic. The optional LLM gray-zone check fails open to the regex result

agents.name: Dispatcher
agents.can: Choose ≤3 intents (payments, cards, general, escalation, off_topic), urgency, sentiment, action_requested, per-intent sub-questions
agents.cannot: Call tools or answer. Deterministic triggers override it
agents.failure: LLM error ⇒ keyword fallback + escalation; low confidence ⇒ add escalation

agents.name: Payments agent
agents.can: Read the ledger and transfers, verify, file a dispute, reverse a fee, cancel a pending transfer, open a ticket on request
agents.cannot: Choose whose data to read, act unasked, act without a matching verification, block cards, claim an action that was not done
agents.tools: get_accounts, get_transactions, get_transaction_detail, get_transfer_status, get_policy, query_knowledge_graph, verify_transaction_issue, file_dispute, reverse_fee, cancel_transfer, search_knowledge_base, get_service_status, create_ticket
agents.failure: Exception ⇒ becomes a needs_human output; ≤4 iterations

agents.name: Cards & fraud agent
agents.can: Read cards, transactions and fraud alerts, verify, block a card, file an unauthorised-payment dispute, order a replacement
agents.cannot: Move money other than through a verified dispute, reverse fees or cancel transfers
agents.tools: get_cards, get_fraud_alerts, get_transactions, get_transaction_detail, get_accounts, get_policy, query_knowledge_graph, verify_transaction_issue, file_dispute, block_card, request_replacement_card, search_knowledge_base, get_service_status, create_ticket

agents.name: General agent
agents.can: Answer product, policy and how-to questions from the help articles and the policy table
agents.cannot: Read account data beyond the profile; no write tools

agents.name: Escalation agent
agents.can: Read ticket history, write the handoff note, create the review row
agents.cannot: Resolve the issue, promise outcomes, admit fault, lower the deterministic priority floor
agents.failure: LLM error ⇒ template note; tool error ⇒ safe holding message. Escalation never fails

agents.name: Validator
agents.can: approve / request one revision / send to a human
agents.cannot: Edit the reply, call write tools, fall back to a weaker model

agents.name: Human (staff)
agents.can: Approve, edit or reject a held draft; approve or reject a pending provisional credit
agents.cannot: Be bypassed for disputes above the auto limit or for held drafts
agents.tools: review-queue API / Slack buttons (agent_staff, admin roles)
agents.failure: Case stays pending (see gaps: no SLA timer yet)

nodes: dispatcher ‖ safety model (advisory) ‖ KB warm-up (parallel, then joined)
fan-out: ≤2 specialists + escalation in parallel (LangGraph Send)
each specialist: staged prefetch → ledger → verify → action → ReAct answer
deliver | revise (≤1, with the actions already done carried forward) | human_prepare → human_wait (interrupt) → human_resolve
rules: Graph state is checkpointed (SQLite) so a paused human-review run survives restarts
Hard caps: 4 ReAct iterations, 12 tool calls, 1 revision, 60 s request timeout
Any unhandled error ⇒ safe fallback: holding reply + review row
Validated KB-only answers can be served from an exact-match cache (no LLM calls)
Verification is idempotent within a query, so a revision cannot contradict the action the first attempt took

state.meaning: Identity of the run; customer_id comes from the JWT
Raw text, and the sanitised text agents may see (secrets and cards masked)
Guard verdict: reasons, injection score, patterns, foreign ids
Intents, urgency, sentiment, confidence, action_requested, sub-questions, forced escalation reasons
Actions (and their verifications) done by an earlier attempt, carried into the revision
What the customer sees and why
Every investigation: tables, policies, graph paths and articles consulted, the checks, the decision

zones.rule: JWT, role, rate limit, body size, schema; the customer id is taken from the token only
Deterministic filters before any model sees text
May be manipulated; hold no credentials; their outputs are proposals, not actions
Allow-list, schemas, SQLi scan, identity injection, intent-gated writes, verification required for actions, budgets, audit
Parameterised queries scoped by customer id; policies and graph are data; internal columns (risk flag, fraud score) never leave the tool layer
Role-checked endpoints; Slack requests signature-verified with replay window; only linked staff can use review buttons

boundaries: Customer text → agents: only through the input guard, always framed as untrusted data
Agent → tool: only through the tool runtime
Tool → database: only parameterised, customer-scoped queries
Agent → customer: only through the validator
Internal risk information → customer: never (tool filter + output guard)
Staff → system: only through role-checked endpoints
Logs / traces / Slack: PII and card data masked before write

policies.rule: The model never chooses whose data is read; customer_id is injected from the session and a different one is blocked and logged
Each agent has an allow-list of tools; write tools are further gated
Disputes, fee reversals and transfer cancellations need a matching verification record that is re-derived at action time
Eligibility and amounts come from the policy table through code; above the provisional-credit limit a human approves; writes are idempotent and audited
Disputes, reversals, cancellations, blocks, replacements and tickets only when the customer asked
Input guard (regex noisy-OR, gray-zone LLM check), topic control, untrusted-text framing
Card numbers, SSN, IBAN and API keys are masked before any model sees them or anything is stored
Every amount, date, id and number-with-unit in a reply must exist in the evidence; unsupported 'does not support X' claims are blocked
'Credit issued', 'dispute filed', 'card blocked', 'transfer cancelled' only if the matching tool succeeded; promises of actions that were not performed are blocked
AML / compliance reviews, risk flags and fraud scores never reach a customer
Other customers' ids, internal tool names, prompt text, raw metadata never reach a reply
Validator or judge unavailable ⇒ human review, never an unverified answer; the judge never uses a weaker fallback model
Every write and every blocked call is in audit_log / security_events; every decision is traced with PII masked
JWT with roles and expiry, login lockout, rate limits, body-size cap, generic 500s, scoped data views

failures.behaviour: Retry with backoff; hedged request; fallback model (not for the validator); circuit breaker for retired models
Circuit breaker skips it; fallbacks serve; validator fails closed
failures.customer_sees: Answers continue; harder cases go to a human

failures.failure: A tool errors or is blocked
failures.behaviour: Error text returned to the model to repair; blocked calls are logged
failures.customer_sees: A corrected answer, or an explanation

failures.failure: Verification says 'human' (stale hold, return not credited, overdue transfer, over-limit fee, internal flag)
failures.behaviour: Deterministic hand-off whatever the model wrote
failures.customer_sees: A short holding message with a reference (never the reason when it is internal)

failures.failure: Verification missing a check the graph names
failures.behaviour: The decision falls back to human review and never auto-approves
Agent says it couldn't find it; needs_human
One revision with the exact issues and the actions already done; then human review
failures.human_sees: Draft and issues in the packet

failures.failure: Safety model unreachable or false-positive on banking words
failures.behaviour: Unreachable: continue without it. Flags a confident banking request: advisory only (logged), no escalation
Alert dropped; the queue still holds the case
failures.human_sees: Case visible in the UI / API

failures.behaviour: Transient lock retried; atomic id allocation

gaps: There is no real payment rail or core-banking system behind the tools: a provisional credit or a reversal is a ledger entry in a synthetic database, not a movement of money.
Account balances are seeded plus the posted ledger; they are not a full double-entry accounting system.
Only duplicate and unauthorised disputes are automated; goods-not-received and wrong-amount disputes go to a human.
Pending reviews have no SLA timer, so nobody is alerted if staff never respond.
The fraud engine is simulated (fixed signals); the agents never see its scores.
Escalation holding replies are English only.
The rate limiter and answer cache are per process; SQLite is single-writer (Postgres/Redis for scale).
The judge and the specialists are the same model family, so shared blind spots are possible.
The general-purpose safety model over-flags banking vocabulary, so its verdict is advisory for confident banking requests.
